checks.name: Event listeners are cleaned up
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');const exts=['.ts','.tsx'];const bad=[];function walk(d){for(const e of fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true})){const p=path.join(d,e.name);if(e.isDirectory())walk(p);else if(exts.includes(path.extname(p))&&!p.includes('.test.')){const s=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');const adds=(s.match(/addEventListener\s*\(/g)||[]).length;const rems=(s.match(/removeEventListener\s*\(/g)||[]).length;if(adds>rems)bad.push(p)}}}for(const d of ['UI','utils'])if(fs.existsSync(d))walk(d);if(bad.length){console.error('Event listeners added without matching removeEventListener: '+bad.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('Event listeners are paired with cleanup.')"

cannotTest: Code duplication, general technical debt, algorithmic efficiency, render/memoisation quality, and whether resource usage is actually minimal on a low-spec device cannot be decided by regexes or a shell command and need reviewer judgement. The listener check only compares addEventListener and removeEventListener counts within a single non-test file; it cannot prove cleanup is correct, nor detect leaks from timers, subscriptions, observers, module-level caches or closures, and a deliberate add here/remove there split across files would be flagged. Busy-wait, dynamic-execution and unsafe-HTML checks only cover the literal forms matched by their regexes (aliases, wrappers and multi-line constructions are out of scope), and the JSON deep-clone check flags a shortcut pattern rather than measuring performance.
